title: Commitment Thaw Controller and Grace Period Allocator
author: Evelyn Chen
release_notes: Introduce a Commitment Thaw Controller that allows recently-decommitted tenant reservations to temporarily re-claim capacity during short overcommit spikes. Adds telemetry and a configurable grace window.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces the Commitment Thaw Controller and a companion Grace Period Allocator to reduce unnecessary permanent revocations of committed capacity during brief, transient overcommit spikes. Motivation: customers on Dedicated often see allocation churn when short-lived surges cause the autoscaler to decommit reservation commitments aggressively. Permanently revoking commitments for a tenant when the pressure is transient causes increased tail latency and unnecessary warm-up cost when the tenant soon needs capacity again. The goal here is to give recently-decommitted commitments a short, configurable thaw window during which they may be re-bound without counting as a new cold allocation.

What changed (high level):
- New controller: redwood/pkg/autoscaler/thaw_controller.go — reconciles decommitted reservations, tracks 'thaw tokens' per-tenant, and exposes an API to attempt 'thaw binds' that prefer recently-held reservations for a short grace period.
- Allocation layer: redwood/internal/allocator/grace_allocator.go — decorator over existing allocator that observes thaw tokens and prefers soft reclaims when within the grace window.
- API surface: reservation.proto updated with two optional fields: thaw_token and thaw_expires_at (RFC3339 string). Reservation manager persists thaw metadata to existing reservation store (no schema migration required — stored as reservation metadata map).
- Telemetry: new metrics and events added (reservation_thaw_attempts_total, reservation_thaw_success_total, reservation_thaw_failure_reason_count, reservation_grace_active_gauge). Added traces for thaw attempts (tagged by tenant_id, cause).
- Config flags: console and dedicated config: dedicated.autoscaler.commitment_thaw_window (default 30s), dedicated.autoscaler.max_thaw_reclaims_per_minute.
- Tests: unit tests for controller backoff logic, allocator integration tests, and small e2e in perf-canary verifying behavior under a synthetic 90s spike.
- Docs: Redwood Console docs page (docs/observability/commitment-thaw.md) describing metrics and recommended knobs.

Commits (summary):
- 4 commits: initial controller scaffolding; allocator wiring and proto updates; telemetry and tests; fixes for race in reservation store integration.

Files touched (representative):
- redwood/pkg/autoscaler/thaw_controller.go (+220 additions)
- redwood/internal/allocator/grace_allocator.go (+160)
- proto/reservation.proto (+12)
- internal/storage/reservation_store.go (+36) — small metadata persistence changes
- observability/metrics/registry.go (+18)
- tests/autoscaler/thaw_controller_test.go (+120)
- perf-canary/scenarios/thaw_reclaim_smoke.yaml (+18)
- docs/observability/commitment-thaw.md (+28)
- go.mod / go.sum updated for prometheus client patch

Behavioral notes and design decisions:
- The thaw window is intentionally short (default 30s) and configurable. We ship conservative defaults to avoid gaming where tenants hold thaw tokens indefinitely.
- Thaw tokens are per-tenant, time-limited, and rate-limited (configurable). Reclaims using a thaw token do not count as 'cold allocations' for warmup heuristics.
- We implemented a soft-preference in the allocator: when both a thawable reservation and fresh capacity are available, allocator chooses the thawable reservation until its quota is exhausted or the thaw window expires.
- No schema migration: thaw metadata is stored in the reservation metadata map so older controllers ignore the keys safely.

CI and tests:
- Initial CI run failed (race detected in reservation_store test) — root cause was a map write without lock in the fake store. Fixed by adding proper locking in the test helper and adjusting the controller backoff to avoid tight busy loops.
- Unit coverage added for controller state transitions and allocator preference logic. e2e smoke verifies that a paused tenant regains equivalent capacity without triggering a new reservation allocation metric.
- CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration: pass (perf-canary smoke), lint: pass, e2e: pass.

Review thread (high level):
- Aisha Patel: Asked for clarity on race conditions between allocator preference and eviction. Requested explicit unit test where thaw token expires mid-reclaim. Also asked to expose metric for thaw token churn. Comment: "Add a test where thaw_expires_at is reached during an allocation — we should ensure we don't double-count quota."
- Author (Evelyn): Added thaw expiry test, exposed reservation_thaw_failure_reason_count and documented failure reasons. Updated PR with additional test and minor allocator simplification to check token expiry atomically.
- Marco Reyes: Suggested making the default window shorter (20s) for now; we kept 30s after discussion because some customers exhibited <10s bursts; added a console toggle to override per-deployment.
- Jonas Müller: Noted potential telemetry cardinality and requested tenant_id be a label only on traces and not on Prometheus metrics; changed metrics to use tenant UUID hashed label for low-cardinality and added trace/span attributes with full tenant id.
- Final approvals from Aisha and Marco after small test additions and doc updates.

Backward compatibility and safety:
- The controller is guarded behind a feature flag in dedicated config (enabled by default for this release); the allocator decorator is opt-in via config so we can rollback quickly.
- Metrics added are additive and use low-cardinality labels by default.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: Thaw tokens could be abused to hog freed capacity. Mitigation: rate limits and max_thaw_reclaims_per_minute enforced; tokens expire quickly; allocator prefers thawed reservations but still honors tenant-level throttles and SLA-based admission checks.
- Risk: Increased allocator complexity introduces subtle fairness regressions. Mitigation: added unit/regression tests and a perf-canary scenario to validate fairness under mixed workload.

Merging:
- Squashed and merged to main on 2024-11-13 after CI green and two approvals. Merge method: squash. Merge commit: c4b9f3e2a8d6c1b4f9e2d7a6b3c1f0e5d6a7b8c9.

How to validate in staging:
1) Enable dedicated.autoscaler.commitment_thaw_window on staging and set small limits for max_thaw_reclaims_per_minute.
2) Run perf-canary scenario perf-canary/scenarios/thaw_reclaim_smoke.yaml; observe metrics: reservation_thaw_attempts_total increments on spikes and reservation_thaw_success_total matches expected rebinds.
3) Check that warmup metrics do not increment for thaw-based reclaims (ensures we didn't create cold allocations).

Related work:

- SUP-1873 (customer report that motivated conservative rollout)

Notes for follow-ups:
- Consider exposing tenant-scoped UI in Console to observe active thaw tokens and recent thaw history.
- Explore automatic tuning of thaw window per-tenant based on observed spike duration.
